title: Plum Jam
subtitle: Victoria plum jam, soft, fragrant, and quick to make
excerpt: Victoria plums make a soft-set jam with a gentle floral sweetness. The skins add colour and the stones come out cleanly once the fruit has softened. Makes three to four 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. Victoria plum is the classic British jam plum; stones float and are removed once the fruit has softened.

recipe.freezeNotes: Halved, stoned plums freeze well for out-of-season batches.
recipe.batchNotes: Up to 2 kg fruit at once.

content.text: Plum jam is one of the fastest-cooking stone-fruit preserves. The fruit softens and breaks down quickly, the stones rise to the surface and can be lifted out with a slotted spoon, and the whole batch is done in under 30 minutes. Victoria plums give a warm amber jam with a soft, honeyed sweetness. Makes three to four 450 g jars.

items.prepNote: halved and stoned if possible, or leave whole and remove stones as they float

content.text: Put the plums, water, and lemon juice in the jam pan over medium heat. Stir occasionally and simmer until the fruit is completely soft and the skins are breaking down, about 10 minutes. Scoop out any stones that have risen to the surface with a slotted spoon.

Add the sugar and stir over low heat until completely dissolved. Raise to a full rolling boil and cook without stirring for 10 to 15 minutes. Test on a cold plate from 10 minutes. When the surface wrinkles, remove from the heat, skim, rest 5 minutes, then ladle into hot sterilised jars and seal.

items.cause: Not all stones were removed before jarring.
items.fix: Stir gently before ladling and check for stones. Halving and stoning before cooking prevents this entirely.

items.cause: Overripe or damaged fruit is lower in pectin.
items.fix: Return to the pan and boil for another 5 minutes, or add 1 extra tbsp lemon juice and test again.

items.cause: Cracked stones released the almond kernel during cooking.
items.fix: Stone the fruit before cooking. The bitterness fades over a few weeks in the jar.
Use the widest pan available to speed evaporation and reach setting point in 10 to 15 minutes.
